title: Texas seller disclosure
description: Texas seller disclosure starts with the TREC Seller's Disclosure Notice, which cites Property Code section 5.008. This is not legal advice.
summary: Fill the TREC notice from a written walk. Do not assume your sale is exempt because you are selling it yourself.
body: This is not legal advice. The Texas seller disclosure for a previously occupied single-family home is the [TREC Seller's Disclosure Notice](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/sellers-disclosure-notice). TREC says the form contains information required by Section 5.008 of the Texas Property Code about material facts and the physical condition of the property. Some sales fall outside that requirement. Read the instructions. A house that has nothing wrong is not the exception. An estate, a new house, or a foreclosure might be. Ask a Texas lawyer if you are not sure.

Fill the notice from the prep walk, with old repair bills beside you. Foundation work, water, and systems that do not work are the lines people regret rushing. Known facts stay known after you paint. If you learn something material before closing, ask your lawyer or broker whether a correction is required. Do not wait out a buyer's option period hoping they skip the attic.

Selling without an agent does not delete the notice. The job list in [Realtor vs FSBO](/tips/list-the-jobs-before-you-choose) still needs a name on the disclosure line, and in Texas that name is often you. Give buyers the completed notice with the contract papers your lawyer or broker tells you to use. A verbal tour is not the notice.

Keep a copy in the closing folder. The national records habit applies: the form is part of what you signed. If a question does not match the house, do not force a no. Attach an explanation a stranger can read. The Texas guide is the full checklist. This note is only the disclosure. Save the signed notice with the contract so you can see what you delivered if a question comes up later.
steps: Download the current TREC Seller's Disclosure Notice and read the instructions.
Walk the house and gather repair records before you answer.
Ask a Texas lawyer if you think the notice might not apply.
Deliver the completed notice. Do not rely on a conversation.
Update it if you learn a new material fact, after you ask whether you must.

title: Cost of selling a house in Texas
description: The cost of selling a house in Texas is your title quote, your payoff, and the compensation you negotiate. Do not use a guessed percent.
summary: Add the written quotes. A percent you heard at a party is not a line on the statement.
body: The cost of selling a house in Texas is a stack of quotes, not a statewide rate. This is not legal advice. Get a title-company estimate, a mortgage payoff quote if a loan remains, and any broker compensation in writing. Type those figures into the [net proceeds calculator](/tools/net-proceeds). Read [Seller closing costs: what sellers pay](/tips/seller-closing-costs) so you recognize payoff, prorations, and credits. That national page is the glossary. Your estimate is the dollars.

Ask who pays for the owner's title policy in the contract you will sign. Custom is not the contract. Survey, HOA resale documents, and repair credits are separate lines. Add them when you have a number. Do not also subtract a guessed percent on top of a real commission quote. That counts the broker twice.

A typical range is the wrong tool for Texas title insurance, because the policy you buy has a quoted premium. Call the title company and ask for the estimate at your price. Compensation to a broker is negotiated. The [commission comparison](/tools/commission) uses the rates you type. [Realtor commission changes](/tips/realtor-commission-changes) is the national note on that negotiation. Nothing on this page sets a fee.

If the net is less than the payoff, read the note on selling before the mortgage is paid off before you list. A Texas sale does not waive a shortage. The statement at the end is still the authority. An estimate from month one can move. Read the draft when it arrives. Ask the title company to refresh the estimate if the price changes, and replace the old figure in the calculator. Keep the older estimate so you can see what moved, and use only the current written quote in the calculator.
steps: Request a written title estimate at your likely price.
Order the loan payoff through the closing date.
Write broker compensation only from a quote you received.
Put those figures in the net calculator. Do not add a guessed percent.
Match the final statement to the quotes before you sign.

title: Seller closing costs Texas
description: Seller closing costs Texas follow your contract and title quote. Use the national seller-closing-costs note to read the lines, then match the dollars.
summary: The categories match a sale anywhere. The amounts are the Texas quote and the contract you signed.
body: This is not legal advice. Seller closing costs Texas are the seller's column on your settlement statement. [Seller closing costs: what sellers pay](/tips/seller-closing-costs) explains the kinds of lines: the mortgage payoff, broker compensation you agreed to, title and escrow charges the contract assigns to you, prorations, and credits. Use that page as the glossary. Then put your title company's estimate next to it so the vocabulary has Texas dollars.

Read who pays the owner's title policy. If the contract says you pay it, it stays in your column even if you heard that buyers always pay it. If the contract says the buyer pays it, do not subtract it twice out of habit. Survey and HOA fees belong on the estimate only when this sale has them. A repair credit you countered is a cost. A repair you only thought about is not.

The payoff quote must still be in date. Texas closings do not get a special rule that freezes interest. If the quote expired, order another before you treat the proceeds as final. Confirm any wire on a phone number you already had. The closing guide's wire rule is national and it applies on a Texas file. Report a swapped instruction at [FBI IC3](https://www.ic3.gov/).

Bring the draft statement home the day it arrives, not to the appointment. Circle any line that is not in the contract or the quotes. Ask the closer to trace it. Signing because the buyer is in the lobby is how a fee you never agreed to becomes yours. If a line names a fee you did not agree to, ask for the contract paragraph before you treat it as final. Circle it and wait for the answer before the appointment, not in the lobby.
steps: Read the national seller-closing-costs note for the categories.
Lay your title estimate on top of those categories.
Check the contract line that assigns the owner's title policy.
Refresh the payoff if it expires.
Question every new line on the draft statement before you sign.

title: Selling a house in Texas without a realtor
description: Selling a house in Texas without a realtor still needs the disclosure and a contract a title company can close. Ask a Texas lawyer which form to use.
summary: You may sell without a broker. License holders must use TREC forms. You should ask a lawyer which contract to sign.
body: This is not legal advice. Selling a house in Texas without a realtor is allowed. It is not informal. The [Texas Real Estate Commission](https://www.trec.texas.gov/) requires license holders to use promulgated contract forms, and those forms are public records you can read on the [contracts page](https://www.trec.texas.gov/agency-information/contracts). If you are not a license holder, do not invent a form and do not borrow one from another state. Ask a Texas real estate lawyer which contract to use and to review the offer before you sign.

You still complete the seller disclosure when the law requires it for this house. You still need showing hours you can keep. [FSBO showings](/tips/plan-showing-hours-before-you-advertise) and [Selling a house by owner](/tips/questions-if-you-sell-it-yourself) are the national notes for hours and questions. They do not name the Texas form. Put a lawyer's fee in the budget. A typical range is whatever that lawyer quotes for one review. Ask. A few hundred dollars is a different job from an estate dispute.

Pick the title company on purpose and save its phone number before any buyer emails you wire instructions. Compensation to a buyer's broker, if you offer it, is a written choice. Put the quotes in the commission tool. Nothing here sets a rate. Read the option period on the offer. It is the number of days in that offer, not a statewide constant. During that period the buyer may have a termination right. Know it before you spend their option fee in your head.
The job list is the same as any FSBO sale, with Texas paper inserted. If a line has no name, it will land on you the week the offer arrives. Write the names this weekend.
steps: Read the TREC contract page and ask a Texas lawyer which form you should sign.
Complete the seller disclosure if it applies.
Choose a title company and save a phone number you can call.
Write showing hours and who answers buyers.
Review the option period and any broker pay before you accept.

title: Steps to selling a house in Texas
description: Steps to selling a house in Texas: walk the house, complete the TREC disclosure, price from quotes, then show, accept, and close on the contract.
summary: Follow the same stage order as any sale, and insert the Texas disclosure and contract checks before you advertise.
body: This is not legal advice. The steps to selling a house in Texas follow the stages on this site, with state papers in the right week. Walk and repair using the prep guide. Fill the [TREC Seller's Disclosure Notice](https://www.trec.texas.gov/forms/sellers-disclosure-notice) from that walk. Price only after you have a payoff quote and a title estimate, using the national [seller closing costs](/tips/seller-closing-costs) page as the glossary and your quotes as the numbers. Photograph the house you disclosed.

Decide who will do the jobs. A broker, if you hire one, works from a listing agreement you have read. If you do not hire one, a Texas lawyer should tell you which contract to use. Show the house on hours you can keep. Read every offer for price, the option period, the closing date, and who pays for the owner's title policy. Compare nets, not headlines. The offers guide is the method.

Close with the wire rule: call a known number before you send money. Deliver possession on the date in the contract, not the weekend the buyer prefers. Forward the mail and keep the disclosure, the contract, and the statement. If the house is in an estate or a trust, do the authority steps in the inherited-house guide before step one of this list. A Texas sale does not skip a missing signer.

None of these steps sets a fee or a tax. Capital gains are in Publication 523 and the tax topic. Foundation cracks go on the disclosure and in the foundation topic. This note is only the order, so the Texas papers are not a surprise on the day the sign goes up. Keep the disclosure, the contract, and the statement together after closing.
steps: Walk the house and complete the TREC disclosure from that list.
Get a payoff quote and a title estimate before you choose a price.
Name who handles the contract: a broker, a lawyer, or both.
Read the option period and the title-policy line on every offer.
Close, confirm any wire by phone, and move on the contract date.
